title: EU Data Act Chapter VII — AI Training Data Access Rights and IoT Data Sharing Provisions (2026)
context: 2026-09-01 engine cycle — EU Data Act (Regulation 2023/2854) entered application September 2025; Chapter VII data-sharing obligations reshape the AI training data landscape for providers who depend on IoT-generated data streams
body: The EU Data Act (Regulation 2023/2854) is now fully applicable, and its Chapter VII data-sharing provisions directly affect AI providers who train or fine-tune models on data generated by connected products. The Act requires that users of IoT devices — from industrial sensors to consumer wearables — can access and share the data those devices generate, including with third parties. For an AI provider, this means three shifts. First, access rights: a provider who wants to train on IoT-generated data must navigate a new statutory framework where the data holder (typically the manufacturer) is obliged to make data available under FRAND terms — gone is the default that the manufacturer owns the exhaust data by possession. Second, fairness conditions: the Act prohibits data holders from using IoT data to derive insights about a user's economic situation and then acting on those insights in a way that harms the user (Article 5(2)), which constrains certain model-training pipelines. Third, switching and interoperability: users can port their data between providers, so a training corpus built on IoT data is not a permanent moat; the data can walk. For a Council of AI verified-measurement operator, the Data Act creates a procurement signal: deployers who arrive with signed, per-axis measurement evidence can demonstrate that their training data access complies with Chapter VII access-right, fairness, and portability obligations, and that their measurement surface covers the data-pipeline boundary — a concrete edge where monitored containment matters. A measurement credential that captures data-ingest provenance, consent-chain logging, and FRAND compliance instrumentation turns the Data Act from a regulatory burden into a verifiable trust signal. Key dates: the Data Act entered application on 12 September 2025; Member State enforcement frameworks are being stood up through 2026. The Commission is expected to publish model contract terms for data sharing under Chapter VII in Q4 2026.
